div.note: Liebermann's base text for 1–15.1 is K (Cotton Claudius A III f. 31v, mid-11th c., after the Latin paraphrase); D (CCCC 201) begins only at 16. ‘K.’ (capitul) stands before each chapter in K. Dated 16 May 1008–13 May 1011. Perhaps VI Atr derives from the same law as V Atr (Liebermann).; AY: added from Rabin p. 160, October 2026 (Rabin’s note to the text); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “16 May 1008 –13 May 1011; 1008 (Robertson, Wormald); Enham”, now “16 May 1008–13 May 1011 (Liebermann); 1008 (Robertson, Wormald); Enham”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “16 May 1008–13 May 1011 (Liebermann); 1008 (Robertson, Wormald); Enham”, now “16 May 1008–13 May 1011 (Liebermann, I p. 246); 1008 (Robertson; Wormald, MEL pp. 332–5); Enham”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “K 246; German 246”; 96 rows of VI Atr); V: page of the modern editor’s text / translation, checked against Robertson (translation on the facing page), October 2026 (e.g. was “90”, now “90 / 91”; 96 rows of VI Atr); AX: pages in Rabin (text / translation), checked against Rabin (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “160”, now “160 / 161”; 5 rows of VI Atr)
Manuscripts: K = London, Cotton MS Claudius A.iii, fols. 35v–37r.

note.seg: Hs. Cotton Claudius A III (einst im Dom zu Canterbury) f. 33ᵇ, hinter der Lateinischen Paraphrase (s. folgende Seite), Mitte XI. Jahrhunderts.
MS Cotton Claudius A III (once in the cathedral at Canterbury) f. 33b, after the Latin paraphrase (see next page), mid-11th century.

Vielleicht entfloss VI Atr. nur demselben Gesetz wie V Atr.; zu letzterem näher als zu VI Atr. steht, was X Atr. Prol. 3 als Gesetz æt Eanham, wo doch VI Atr. (laut der Paraphrase) erging, citiert; vgl. o. S. 236, Sp. 1**.

Perhaps VI Atr. derived only from the same law as V Atr.; what X Atr. Prol. 3 cites as the law æt Eanham, where VI Atr. (according to the Paraphrase) was after all issued, stands closer to the latter than to VI Atr.; cf. above p. 236, col. 1**.
[Die Buchstabennoten beziehen sich auf die Lateinische Paraphrase.] synodalis hier und 40, 2 nicht ‘geistlich-synodal’, sondern ‘reichstäglich’; s. Einl. 15. 19
[The letter notes refer to the Latin paraphrase.] synodalis here and in 40, 2 means not ‘ecclesiastical-synodal’ but ‘of the national assembly’; see Introduction 15. 19
